definition: a group of people, often related, who share the same culture, language, and traditions

collocations.example: The nomadic tribe moved across the desert each season.
She is a respected member of the tribe.

definition: to cause something to start or happen suddenly

collocations.example: Certain foods can trigger a severe allergic reaction.
Opening the door may trigger the security alarm.

definition: a great victory or success, and the joy that comes with it

collocations.example: The project was a great triumph for the team.
The winning team returned home in triumph.

definition: soldiers, especially a large organized group of them

collocations.example: The troop withdrawal began after the peace agreement.
The government decided to deploy troops to the border.

definition: a long hollow cylinder, or a soft container, used to hold or carry a substance

collocations.example: I bought a new tube of toothpaste today.
The chemist poured the liquid into a test tube.

definition: an underground or underwater passage for a road, railway, or people

collocations.example: The train disappeared into the long railway tunnel.
Workers began to dig a tunnel through the mountain.

definition: being the final or most important thing of its kind

collocations.example: Our ultimate goal is to expand into new markets.
The manager holds ultimate responsibility for the decision.

definition: to experience something, especially a change or medical treatment

collocations.example: She will undergo surgery on her knee next week.
The company will undergo major changes this year.

definition: to be the hidden cause or basis of something

collocations.example: Several assumptions underlie the entire business plan.
These core ideas underlie much of his later work.

definition: to take on a task or responsibility and begin doing it

collocations.example: The university will undertake research into renewable energy.
She agreed to undertake the difficult task alone.

definition: a special set of clothes worn by members of a group or organization

collocations.example: All students must wear a school uniform here.
Nurses in this hospital wear a blue uniform.

definition: being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else

collocations.example: This is a unique opportunity to study abroad.
The phone has one truly unique feature.

definition: the state of being joined together as one; agreement

collocations.example: The leader called for greater national unity.
The festival created a strong sense of unity.

definition: all of space and everything that exists in it

collocations.example: Scientists study how the expanding universe behaves over time.
Many theories explain the origin of the universe.

definition: to add the most recent information or improve something

collocations.example: Please update the software to the latest version.
You should update your details on the website.

definition: relating to a town or city rather than the countryside

collocations.example: Traffic is heavy in most urban areas.
The council approved a new urban development plan.

definition: to strongly advise or encourage someone to do something

collocations.example: Experts urge caution when investing in new markets.
Doctors urge patients to exercise more regularly.

definition: needing immediate attention or action

collocations.example: There is an urgent need for clean water.
She left an urgent message for the director.

definition: a basic public service such as water, gas, or electricity

collocations.example: Our utility bills are higher during the winter.
The water company is a regulated public utility.

definition: not clear or definite in meaning or detail

collocations.example: I only had a vague idea of the plan.
The witness gave a very vague description.

definition: legally or officially acceptable and able to be used

collocations.example: This ticket is valid for three months.
Both parties signed a legally valid contract.

definition: a number of different types of things within one group

collocations.example: The store offers a wide variety of goods.
The shop stocks a variety of imported cheeses.

definition: extremely large in size, amount, or extent

collocations.example: The vast majority of staff supported the change.
The project required a vast amount of money.

definition: a new business project that involves risk

collocations.example: The two firms formed a joint venture overseas.
His latest business venture proved very profitable.

definition: used to show two sides competing against or being compared with each other

collocations.example: Tonight's final pits the underdogs versus the champions.
Buyers often weigh quality versus price before deciding.

definition: a ship or large boat used to carry people or goods

collocations.example: A small fishing vessel entered the busy harbor.
The cargo vessel carried oil across the ocean.

definition: a person with long experience in a particular field or activity

collocations.example: A veteran employee trained all the new staff.
She is an industry veteran with thirty years of experience.

definition: by means of a particular person, system, or method

collocations.example: Customers can book their tickets via the website.
She sent the report to her manager via email.

definition: an immoral or unhealthy habit

collocations.example: Greed can become a truly terrible vice.
The novel describes a city that indulged in vice.

definition: success in defeating an opponent in a contest or war

collocations.example: The team secured a narrow victory on Saturday.
The candidate was quick to claim victory.

definition: to break or fail to obey a law, rule, or agreement

collocations.example: Companies that violate the law face heavy fines.
Players who violate the rules are removed immediately.

definition: behavior that uses physical force to hurt or damage someone or something

collocations.example: The charity helps victims of domestic violence.
The protest ended without a single act of violence.

definition: created or simulated by a computer rather than existing physically

collocations.example: The museum offers a virtual reality tour.
The team held a virtual meeting across three countries.

definition: a good moral quality in a person

collocations.example: Patience is a virtue in any good teacher.
Honesty is a rare virtue in politics.

definition: a tiny agent that causes disease in the body

collocations.example: A new flu virus spread quickly this winter.
He caught a virus and stayed home sick.

definition: able to be seen

collocations.example: The mountains were clearly visible from the beach.
He showed no visible sign of nervousness.

definition: the ability to see

collocations.example: The patient complained of sudden blurred vision.
Cats have excellent night vision in the dark.

definition: relating to seeing or to things that can be seen

collocations.example: The bold design has a strong visual impact.
The teacher used visual aids during the lesson.

definition: extremely important and necessary for success or survival

collocations.example: Nurses play a vital role in patient recovery.
Clean water is of vital importance to health.

definition: the level of loudness of a sound

collocations.example: Please turn down the volume on the radio.
The volume control on this speaker is broken.

definition: done willingly, without being forced or paid

collocations.example: Each member made a small voluntary contribution.
She helps at the shelter on a voluntary basis.

definition: a person who offers to do something without being paid

collocations.example: She does volunteer work at the local library.
The organizer asked for a willing volunteer.

definition: easily harmed, hurt, or attacked

collocations.example: The policy aims to protect vulnerable groups in society.
Young plants are vulnerable to sudden frost.

definition: a large amount of money and valuable possessions

collocations.example: His personal wealth grew rapidly over the decade.
The bank offers wealth management to its clients.

definition: to make cloth or an object by crossing threads or strips over and under each other

collocations.example: The villagers still weave cloth by hand.
She learned to weave a basket from dried reeds.

definition: to have a particular weight

collocations.example: Each box can weigh several kilos when full.
These stone blocks each weigh almost a ton.

definition: the health, happiness, and general wellbeing of a person or group

collocations.example: The agency is responsible for child welfare.
The company cares about the welfare of its staff.

definition: a very quiet way of speaking using the breath rather than the voice

collocations.example: She told me the secret in a whisper.
His voice dropped to a soft whisper.

definition: to pull out of or remove from an activity or place

collocations.example: An injury forced her to withdraw from the race.
The government agreed to withdraw troops from the region.

definition: to produce or provide a result, profit, or amount

collocations.example: The investment should yield a healthy profit.
The new strategy began to yield results quickly.

definition: the period of life when a person is young

collocations.example: He was a fine athlete in his youth.
He jokingly blamed his bad habits on a misspent youth.

definition: an area that is different from those around it or used for a particular purpose

collocations.example: New York is in a different time zone.
Rescue teams rushed into the disaster zone.

definition: not normal, usual, or expected

collocations.example: The doctor noticed some abnormal behavior in the patient.
Tests revealed an abnormal condition in his blood.

definition: on or onto a ship, plane, train, or bus

collocations.example: All the passengers were already aboard the ship.
The inspector checked every passenger aboard the train.

definition: sudden and unexpected

collocations.example: There was an abrupt change in the weather.
The car came to an abrupt halt.

definition: not present in a place where one is expected to be

collocations.example: He was absent from work for three days.
The student was frequently absent during the term.

definition: completely unreasonable, illogical, or ridiculous

collocations.example: Leaving the company now would be an absurd idea.
His excuse began to sound absurd.

definition: a person whose job is to keep and check financial records

collocations.example: She hired a chartered accountant for the business.
The chief accountant reviewed the annual budget.

definition: to make oneself or someone familiar with something new

collocations.example: It took weeks to accustom herself to the heat.
It takes a moment to accustom your eyes to the dark.

definition: a chemical substance with a sour taste that can react with and damage other materials

collocations.example: Acid rain has damaged many ancient statues.
Lemons contain a large amount of citric acid.

definition: to make someone familiar with something

collocations.example: Please acquaint yourself with the safety rules first.
The guide will acquaint visitors with the museum's history.

definition: to make something start working or become active

collocations.example: Opening this window will activate the alarm.
Enter your code to activate the system.

definition: very serious or severe

collocations.example: There is an acute shortage of nurses.
She felt acute pain in her lower back.

definition: to act according to a rule, agreement, or belief

collocations.example: All members must adhere to the club rules.
The crew tried to adhere to a tight schedule.

definition: next to or very near something else

collocations.example: They waited quietly in an adjacent room.
The car park is adjacent to the station.

definition: to manage or be responsible for the running of something

collocations.example: A small team will administer the new program.
The courts are expected to administer justice fairly.

definition: harmful or unfavorable to something

collocations.example: The drug may have an adverse effect.
The flight was delayed by adverse weather conditions.

definition: relating to beauty or the appreciation of art

collocations.example: The old building has great aesthetic value.
The garden's aesthetic appeal attracts many visitors.

definition: a company or organization connected to a larger one

collocations.example: The bank owns an affiliate company abroad.
The network broadcasts through a local affiliate.

definition: angry or violent feelings or behavior toward others

collocations.example: The invasion was seen as an act of aggression.
The coach does not tolerate physical aggression.

definition: extreme physical or mental pain

collocations.example: He lay on the ground in agony.
The final mile of the race was sheer agony.

definition: to bring into agreement or arrange into the correct position

collocations.example: Our goals must align with the company strategy.
The two departments worked to align their strategies.

definition: in a similar way; to a similar degree

collocations.example: The two colleagues often think alike about budgets.
A good teacher treats all students alike.

definition: a narrow passage or street between or behind buildings

collocations.example: She hurried past a dark alley at night.
The cat disappeared down a narrow back alley.

definition: to happen or occur repeatedly one after the other

collocations.example: Rainy days alternate with bright sunny ones.
She alternates between hope and despair daily.

definition: a light, silvery metal used widely in manufacturing

collocations.example: She wrapped the sandwich in aluminum foil.
The frame is made from a strong aluminum alloy.

definition: a person who does an activity for pleasure, not as a paid professional

collocations.example: As a keen amateur, he photographs birds every weekend.
The painting was produced by a talented amateur.

definition: an official who represents their country in another country

collocations.example: She serves as a goodwill ambassador for the charity.
The British ambassador met the president yesterday.

definition: having more than one possible meaning and so unclear

collocations.example: The reply was deliberately ambiguous to avoid blame.
His ambiguous statement confused the whole committee.

definition: a strong desire to achieve something

collocations.example: Running a marathon was her lifelong ambition.
He finally achieved his ambition of owning a shop.

definition: having a strong desire to be successful

collocations.example: She is a highly ambitious young lawyer.
The ambitious executive aimed for the top job.

definition: a vehicle for taking sick or injured people to hospital

collocations.example: Someone please call an ambulance right now.
The ambulance crew arrived within five minutes.

definition: in the middle of or surrounded by something

collocations.example: She spotted her friend amid the noisy crowd.

definition: a person from whom one is descended, especially from long ago

collocations.example: A distant ancestor of hers sailed to America.

definition: a heavy device dropped into water to hold a ship in place

collocations.example: The crew decided to drop anchor near the island.
The ship lay quietly at anchor overnight.

definition: to give life or energy to something; to make lively

collocations.example: The lively music helped animate the crowd.
Her bold ideas animated the entire debate.

definition: the joint connecting the foot to the leg

collocations.example: He played the match with a sprained ankle.
She spent six weeks recovering from a broken ankle.

definition: the yearly return of the date of a past event

collocations.example: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in Paris.
The company will celebrate its fiftieth anniversary soon.

definition: having a name that is not known or made public

collocations.example: The hospital received money from an anonymous donor.
The witness asked to remain anonymous for safety.

definition: the study of human societies, cultures, and their development

collocations.example: Her thesis focuses mainly on cultural anthropology.
He went to university to study anthropology.

definition: an old object that is valuable because of its age

collocations.example: This clock is a genuine antique from France.
They found the vase in a small antique shop.

definition: relevant or appropriate to a particular person or situation

collocations.example: This rule is not applicable to part-time staff.
Please complete the form where applicable and sign it.

definition: a person who formally asks for something, such as a job

collocations.example: Each job applicant must submit a detailed résumé.
The successful applicant will start work next month.

definition: to assess or judge the value or quality of something

collocations.example: Managers meet yearly to appraise all staff.
She paused to appraise the situation carefully.

definition: a curved structure that spans an opening and supports the weight above it

collocations.example: They walked beneath an ancient stone arch.
The parade passed under the triumphal arch.

definition: a collection of historical documents or records kept for reference

collocations.example: The library holds a vast archive of letters.
Researchers can search the archive for old newspapers.

definition: a large area with seats used for sports or entertainment

collocations.example: The city built a new sports arena downtown.
The band performed before a packed arena.

definition: metal or other hard covering worn to protect the body in battle

collocations.example: The soldiers wore heavy body armor into battle.
A knight's suit of armor stood in the hall.

definition: to cause a feeling or reaction to develop

collocations.example: His sudden wealth began to arouse suspicion.
